name: Accessible Interface Guardrails
description: A sanitised example showing how a community pack can define accessible interface requirements and inspectable acceptance evidence without executable code.

requirements.title: Semantic document structure
requirements.statement: Public interfaces must use meaningful landmarks, headings, labels, and native controls before adding custom interaction behaviour.

requirements.title: Keyboard operation
requirements.statement: Every core journey and interactive control must be usable by keyboard with visible focus and a logical navigation order.

requirements.title: Responsive reflow
requirements.statement: Content and controls must remain understandable and operable across supported viewport sizes without hiding essential actions.

controls.title: Native controls first
controls.purpose: Reduce avoidable accessibility failures by preferring browser-native elements and behaviour before custom widgets.

controls.title: Manual review required
controls.purpose: Prevent automated checks from being presented as complete accessibility assurance without a recorded human review.

guidance: Preserve semantic meaning when visual presentation changes.
Do not remove visible focus indicators without providing an equally clear replacement.
Record limitations and unresolved accessibility decisions rather than claiming unsupported compliance.

acceptance.statement: Recorded evidence demonstrates that every defined core journey can be completed using keyboard input alone.
Automated accessibility findings are resolved or explicitly documented with an owner, reason, and follow-up decision.
